questions.def: Inverted word order after 'not only,' so base form is needed.
questions.question: Not only did he ___ the presentation, but he also answered questions.

questions.def: 'Seldom' requires subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: Seldom ___ such dedication in the workplace.

questions.def: The verb 'lie' agrees with the plural noun 'keys'.
questions.question: There ___ the keys you were looking for.

questions.def: 'So' requires inversion and the adjective 'engaging'.
questions.question: So ___ was the lecture that everyone stayed focused.

questions.def: 'Only' requires inversion and a suitable introductory phrase.
questions.question: Only ___ the data, could we reach a conclusion.

questions.def: Locative inversion: verb precedes subject 'castle'.
questions.question: On the hilltop ___ the ancient castle.

questions.def: In conditional sentences with 'had', subject comes after.
questions.question: Had ___ known, I would have acted differently.

questions.def: 'At no point' requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: At no point ___ his promises.

questions.def: 'Only later' requires the auxiliary verb 'did' for inversion.
questions.question: Only later ___ it clear what had happened.

questions.def: 'Hardly' requires inversion with the auxiliary 'had'.
questions.question: Hardly ___ I arrived when the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Not until' requires inversion with the auxiliary verb.
questions.question: Not until ___ the full picture.

questions.def: 'Little' at the beginning needs subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Little ___ that they were in danger.

questions.def: 'Scarcely' requires inversion with 'had' and past participle.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ the lecture, than the fire alarm rang.

questions.def: Locative inversion: Verb agrees with subject 'actors'.
questions.question: Behind the curtain ___ the actors.

questions.def: In conditional sentences with 'were', subject comes after.
questions.question: Were ___ to decline, the project would be jeopardized.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' demands subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ confidential information.

questions.def: Locative inversion: verb precedes subject 'cottage'.
questions.question: At the end of the road ___ a small cottage.

questions.def: 'Only then' requires subject-auxiliary verb inversion.
questions.question: Only then ___ the truth about the matter.

questions.def: 'So' requires adjective + auxiliary verb + subject order.
questions.question: So ___ that the audience applauded enthusiastically.

questions.def: 'Hardly' needs inverted word order: had + subject.
questions.question: Hardly they had started the meeting when the fire alarm rang.

questions.def: In third conditional, subject follows 'had'.
questions.question: Had ___ the risks, he would have reconsidered.

questions.def: In conditional sentences with 'were', subject comes after.
questions.question: Were ___ to happen again, the consequences would be severe.

questions.def: 'In no way' demands subject-auxiliary inversion.
questions.question: In no way ___ his actions.

questions.def: 'Seldom' in initial position requires inversion of subject and auxiliary verb.
questions.question: Seldom ___ such a blatant disregard for protocol.

questions.def: 'Not only' requires subject-verb inversion in the clause that follows it.
questions.question: Not only ___ the data inaccurate, but it was also incomplete.

questions.def: When a prepositional phrase begins the sentence, invert subject and verb.
questions.question: On the table ___ the missing documents.

questions.def: 'Only after' requires subject-verb inversion in the main clause.
questions.question: Only after extensive research ___ the truth.

questions.def: 'So + adjective' requires inversion of subject and auxiliary verb.
questions.question: So tenuous ___ the connection that it is almost imperceptible.

questions.def: With 'there', the verb agrees with the noun that follows it.
questions.question: There ___ a monument to the fallen soldiers.
